claims.text: Firms seeking deferred payment credit temporary permission must notify the FCA during a specified registration window (15 May 2026 to approximately 1 July 2026) and provide financial projections.

Firms with deferred payment credit temporary permission must achieve full Consumer Duty compliance by Regulation Day (15 July 2026) and apply for full authorisation within 6 months or lose temporary permission.

Before making a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, firms must provide customers with comprehensive key product information (rate, amount, payment schedule, cash price, consequences of non-payment) and additional product information (right to withdraw, credit assessment, adequate explanations, terms).

Immediately after making a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, firms must provide customers with a copy of the agreement and all required product information in a durable medium (unless already provided).

Where guarantors are involved in regulated deferred payment credit agreements, firms must provide adequate explanations and relevant information to enable informed decisions before the agreement is made.
Firms must not unfairly pressure customers to enter regulated deferred payment credit agreements without adequate time to consider the required product information.
As soon as possible after a missed payment on a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, firms must notify the borrower and provide information about adverse consequences and mitigation steps.

Before taking enforcement action (demanding earlier payment, restricting rights, enforcing security) or terminating a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, firms must give reasonable notice; where borrowers are in arrears, firms must also signpost to free debt advice and communicate its benefits.
DPC firms must comply with existing PSD reporting requirements once they exceed de minimis thresholds of £2m in new advances or £2m in outstanding balances.

Firms with only deferred payment credit temporary permission are not SMCR firms; where firms hold both Part 4A permission and DPC temporary permission, the temporary permission is disregarded for SMCR categorisation purposes.
Gibraltar-based firms carrying on deferred payment credit activity must comply with relevant Handbook provisions relating to that activity.

Standard pre-contract disclosure rules (CONC 4.2) and distance marketing rules (CONC 2.7) do not apply to regulated deferred payment credit agreements; instead, specific product information requirements in CONC 4.2A apply.

metadata.note: This analysis extracts proposed binding obligations from consultation materials relating to deferred payment credit regulation. All obligations identified are draft proposals requiring human verification and legal review. The publication signals indicate this is a consultation paper with proposed changes that must not be treated as binding until finalised. Effective dates are based on stated implementation timelines in the consultation. Many rules reference legal instrument pages indicating draft statutory instrument provisions.

candidates.statement: Firms with deferred payment credit temporary permission must notify the FCA of their desire to be registered for the Temporary Permission Regime (TPR) during the notification window opening 15 May 2026 and closing 2 weeks before Regulation Day (15 July 2026).
candidates.sourceQuotation: In line with the proposals in the CP, notification for registration for temporary permission will open 2 months before Regulation Day and close 2 weeks before Regulation Day... notification for registration for the TPR opens on 15 May 2026
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms seeking to enter the Temporary Permission Regime for deferred payment credit activities

candidates.statement: Firms notifying for temporary permission must provide projections of annual income for future DPC activities and projections of the value of their DPC lending when registering.
candidates.sourceQuotation: In CP25/33, in addition to the information referred to in paragraph 5.3, we proposed that firms provide the following information when notifying a desire for registration... A projection of annual income for future DPC activities. • Projections of the value of their DPC lending.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms registering for deferred payment credit temporary permission

candidates.statement: Firms with deferred payment credit temporary permission must be fully compliant with the Consumer Duty from Regulation Day (15 July 2026).
candidates.sourceQuotation: Firms preparing to enter the TPR should begin planning early to ensure operational readiness for Regulation Day. In particular, firms should: • Make sure they are fully compliant with the Consumer Duty from Regulation Day.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms with deferred payment credit temporary permission

candidates.statement: Firms with deferred payment credit temporary permission must apply for full authorisation within 6 months directly following Regulation Day or lose their temporary permission.
candidates.sourceQuotation: Note that temporary permission is not indefinite. Firms will be able to apply for full authorisation before the end of the 6-month window directly following Regulation Day. Firms that do not apply within this window will lose their temporary permission.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms with deferred payment credit temporary permission who wish to continue deferred payment credit activities beyond the temporary permission period

candidates.statement: Before making a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, firms must give to the customer the key product information specified in CONC 4.2A.5R(1) including rate of interest, amount of credit, payment details, cash price, consequences of non-payment, and credit reference agency usage.
candidates.sourceQuotation: Before making an agreement, the firm must: (a) give to the customer the information set out in CONC 4.2A.5R(1) (referred to in this section as the 'key product information')... The key product information referred to in CONC 4.2A.3R(1)(a) is as follows: (a) the rate of interest that applies to the agreement; (b) the amount of the credit to be provided under the agreement...
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms with respect to deferred payment credit lending, before making a regulated deferred payment credit agreement

candidates.statement: Before making a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, firms must give or make available to the customer the additional product information specified in CONC 4.2A.5R(2) including right to withdraw, credit assessment details, adequate explanations, and contractual terms and conditions.
candidates.sourceQuotation: Before making an agreement, the firm must... (b) give, or make available, to the customer the information set out in CONC 4.2A.5R(2) (referred to in this section as the 'additional product information')... The additional product information referred to in CONC 4.2A.3R(1)(b) is as follows...
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms with respect to deferred payment credit lending, before making a regulated deferred payment credit agreement

candidates.statement: Where there is more than one customer acting together as 'joint borrowers', the product information required under CONC 4.2A must be given, or made available, to each customer.
candidates.sourceQuotation: Where there is more than one customer acting together as 'joint borrowers', the information required under this rule must be given, or made available (as applicable), to each customer.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies where a regulated deferred payment credit agreement has joint borrowers

candidates.statement: Immediately after a regulated deferred payment credit agreement has been made, the firm must give, or make available, to the customer in a durable medium a copy of the agreement and the key product information and additional product information (unless already provided).
candidates.sourceQuotation: Immediately after an agreement has been made, the firm must give, or make available, to the customer in a durable medium: (a) a copy of the agreement; and (b) the key product information and the additional product information described in CONC 4.2A.5R.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms with respect to deferred payment credit lending, immediately after making a regulated deferred payment credit agreement

candidates.statement: Where an individual other than the borrower is to provide a guarantee or an indemnity in relation to a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, the firm must, before making the agreement, provide the guarantor with adequate explanations and relevant information to enable an informed decision.
candidates.sourceQuotation: The firm must, before making the agreement, provide the guarantor with the information in (3) in order to place the guarantor in a position to make an informed decision as to whether to act as the guarantor in relation to the agreement.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies where there is a guarantor providing a guarantee or indemnity in relation to a regulated deferred payment credit agreement

candidates.statement: Firms must not unfairly encourage, incentivise or induce a customer to enter into a regulated deferred payment credit agreement quickly without allowing the customer time to consider the information given under CONC 4.2A.3R(1).
candidates.sourceQuotation: A firm must not unfairly encourage, incentivise or induce a customer to enter into a regulated credit agreement quickly without allowing the customer time to consider... (2) in relation to a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, the information given, or made available, to the customer under CONC 4.2A.3R(1).
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms with respect to deferred payment credit lending

candidates.statement: As soon as possible after a borrower has failed to make a payment by the time it has fallen due under a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, the firm must notify the borrower that the missed payment has occurred and provide sufficient information about adverse consequences and steps to mitigate them.
candidates.sourceQuotation: As soon as possible after a missed payment has occurred the firm must: (a) notify the borrower: (i) that the missed payment has occurred... and (b) provide the borrower with sufficient information for the borrower to understand... (ii) any adverse consequences for the borrower arising out of the missed payment...
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies where a borrower has failed to make a payment by the time it has fallen due under a regulated deferred payment credit agreement

candidates.statement: Before a firm takes steps to enforce a term of a regulated deferred payment credit agreement (by demanding earlier payment, restricting rights, or enforcing security) or terminates the agreement, it must give the borrower reasonable notice of its intention to do so.
candidates.sourceQuotation: Before a firm takes any of the actions specified in (2), it must give the borrower reasonable notice of its intention to do so. (2) The actions mentioned in (1) are: (a) taking steps to enforce a term of a regulated deferred payment credit agreement by: (i) demanding the earlier payment of any sum...
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies before taking enforcement action or terminating a regulated deferred payment credit agreement

candidates.statement: Where a firm intends to take enforcement action or terminate a regulated deferred payment credit agreement and the borrower is in arrears, the firm must inform the borrower that free and impartial money guidance and debt advice is available and effectively communicate the potential benefits of accessing it.
candidates.sourceQuotation: Where a firm intends to take any of the actions specified in (2) and the borrower is in arrears, the firm must when giving notice in accordance with (1): (a) inform the borrower that free and impartial money guidance and debt advice is available from not-for-profit debt advice bodies... and (b) effectively communicate to the borrower the potential benefits of accessing money guidance or free and impartial debt advice...
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies where the borrower is in arrears and the firm intends to take enforcement action or terminate a regulated deferred payment credit agreement

candidates.statement: DPC firms must comply with existing regulatory reporting requirements including PSD returns once they breach the de minimis thresholds of either £2m in new advances or £2m in outstanding balances in a given year.
candidates.sourceQuotation: PSD reporting requirements only apply once a firm breaches one of the de minimis thresholds in a given year. Specifically, either £2m in new advances or £2m in outstanding balances.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to DPC firms that breach either £2m in new advances or £2m in outstanding balances in a given year

candidates.statement: In circumstances where the only regulated activities in a firm's permission are deferred payment credit activities permitted by a deferred payment credit temporary permission, the firm is not an SMCR firm.
candidates.sourceQuotation: In circumstances where the only regulated activities in a firm's permission are deferred payment credit activities permitted by a deferred payment credit temporary permission, a firm is not an SMCR firm (and is included in Part Three of SYSC 23 Annex 1 (Definition of exempt firm)).
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies where the only regulated activities in a firm's permission are deferred payment credit activities permitted by deferred payment credit temporary permission

candidates.statement: Where a firm's permission comprises permission granted by the FCA under Part 4A and a deferred payment credit temporary permission, the firm's deferred payment credit temporary permission is to be disregarded for the purposes of categorising what type of SMCR firm the firm is.
candidates.sourceQuotation: The firm's deferred payment credit temporary permission is to be disregarded for the purposes of categorising what type of SMCR firm the firm is in accordance with SYSC 23 Annex 1 (Definition of SMCR firm and different types of SMCR firms).
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies where a firm's permission comprises both Part 4A permission and deferred payment credit temporary permission

candidates.statement: A Gibraltar-based firm carrying on deferred payment credit activity must comply with the relevant Handbook provisions relating to deferred payment credit activity.
candidates.sourceQuotation: A Gibraltar-based firm carrying on deferred payment credit activity must comply with the relevant Handbook provisions relating to deferred payment credit activity.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to Gibraltar-based firms carrying on deferred payment credit activity

candidates.statement: Firms must explain the key features of a regulated credit agreement to enable the customer to make an informed choice as required by CONC 4.2.5R (adequate explanations), but in relation to regulated deferred payment credit agreements, firms must instead provide the information required by CONC 4.2A.3R.
candidates.sourceQuotation: A In relation to a regulated credit agreement other than a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, a firm must explain the key features of a regulated credit agreement to enable the customer to make an informed choice as required by CONC 4.2.5R (adequate explanations)... (2) In relation to a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, a firm must provide the information required by CONC 4.2A.3R.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms conducting business relating to regulated credit agreements and regulated deferred payment credit agreements

candidates.statement: CONC 2.7 (Distance marketing) does not apply to any distance marketing activity carried on in relation to a regulated deferred payment credit agreement.
candidates.sourceQuotation: (4) This section does not apply to any distance marketing activity carried on in relation to a regulated deferred payment credit agreement.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to distance marketing activities relating to regulated deferred payment credit agreements

candidates.statement: CONC 4.2 (Pre-contract disclosure and adequate explanations) does not apply to a regulated deferred payment credit agreement.
candidates.sourceQuotation: This section, unless otherwise stated in or in relation to a rule... (4A) does not apply to a regulated deferred payment credit agreement
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to regulated deferred payment credit agreements

claims.text: Before making a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, firms must give key product information to customers including interest rate, credit amount, payment details, cash price, consequences of non-payment, credit reference checks, and withdrawal rights.

Before making a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, firms must give or make available additional product information including adequate explanations, rights and obligations, withdrawal details, continuous payment authority information, and contractual terms.

Immediately after making a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, firms must provide customers with a copy of the agreement and product information in a durable medium (unless already provided).
Product information must be provided to each customer where there are joint borrowers under a regulated deferred payment credit agreement.

Where a guarantor is involved, firms must provide adequate explanations to the guarantor before making the agreement, covering circumstances when the guarantee might be called and implications for the guarantor.
Firms must communicate with borrowers as soon as possible after a missed payment, including information about adverse consequences.

Before terminating an agreement or taking enforcement action where a customer is in arrears, firms must provide reasonable notice and signpost to free debt advice, communicating the benefits of accessing it.
Information made available to customers must be accessible, clearly signposted, not obscured, and provided in good time for effective decision-making.

Firms with deferred payment credit activities will be subject to Product Sales Data (PSD) reporting requirements once they breach de minimis thresholds of £2m in new advances or £2m in outstanding balances.

Firms must notify the FCA between 15 May 2026 and two weeks before Regulation Day (15 July 2026) to register for temporary permission, paying a Category 1 fee and providing income and lending projections.
Firms with temporary permission must comply with the Consumer Duty from Regulation Day (15 July 2026), including fair value and good customer outcomes.
Firms with temporary permission must apply for full authorisation within 6 months of Regulation Day or lose their temporary permission.
Where a firm holds both Part 4A permission and deferred payment credit temporary permission, the temporary permission is disregarded for SMCR categorisation purposes.
Firms with only deferred payment credit temporary permission are not SMCR firms.
Gibraltar-based firms carrying on deferred payment credit activity must comply with relevant Handbook provisions including product information requirements.

candidates.statement: Before making a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, firms must give to the customer the key product information specified in CONC 4.2A.5R(1), which includes: the interest rate, credit amount, payment frequency and number, payment amounts, cash price of goods/services, consequences of non-payment (including late payment charges and credit rating impacts), whether credit reference agency checks will be performed, and the customer's right to withdraw.
candidates.sourceQuotation: Before making an agreement, the firm must: (a) give to the customer the information set out in CONC 4.2A.5R(1) (referred to in this section as the 'key product information')... The key product information referred to in CONC 4.2A.3R(1)(a) is as follows: (a) the rate of interest that applies to the agreement; (b) the amount of the credit to be provided under the agreement...
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms with respect to deferred payment credit lending, in relation to regulated deferred payment credit agreements

candidates.statement: Before making a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, firms must give or make available to the customer the additional product information specified in CONC 4.2A.5R(2), which includes: an adequate explanation of the key features, the customer's rights and obligations, the right to withdraw and how to exercise it, details of continuous payment authorities (where applicable), and the contractual terms and conditions.
candidates.sourceQuotation: Before making an agreement, the firm must: ... (b) give, or make available, to the customer the information set out in CONC 4.2A.5R(2) (referred to in this section as the 'additional product information')... The additional product information referred to in CONC 4.2A.3R(1)(b) is as follows: (a) an adequate explanation of the key features of the agreement... (i) the contractual terms and conditions.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms with respect to deferred payment credit lending, in relation to regulated deferred payment credit agreements

candidates.statement: Immediately after a regulated deferred payment credit agreement has been made, firms must give or make available to the customer in a durable medium: a copy of the agreement, and the key product information and additional product information (unless already provided in a durable medium or included in the copy of the agreement).
candidates.sourceQuotation: Immediately after an agreement has been made, the firm must give, or make available, to the customer in a durable medium: (a) a copy of the agreement; and (b) the key product information and the additional product information described in CONC 4.2A.5R.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms with respect to deferred payment credit lending, in relation to regulated deferred payment credit agreements

candidates.statement: Where there is more than one customer acting together as joint borrowers, the product information must be given or made available to each customer.
candidates.sourceQuotation: Where there is more than one customer acting together as 'joint borrowers', the information required under this rule must be given, or made available (as applicable), to each customer.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies where there is more than one customer acting together as joint borrowers under a regulated deferred payment credit agreement

candidates.statement: Before entering into a regulated deferred payment credit agreement where an individual other than the borrower is to provide a guarantee or indemnity, firms must provide the guarantor with an adequate explanation of: the circumstances in which the guarantee/indemnity might be called on, the implications for the guarantor, and such other information as necessary for the guarantor to make an informed decision.
candidates.sourceQuotation: The firm must, before making the agreement, provide the guarantor with the information in (3) in order to place the guarantor in a position to make an informed decision as to whether to act as the guarantor... The information referred to in (2) is: (a) an adequate explanation of: (i) the circumstances in which the guarantee or the indemnity (or both) might be called on; and (ii) the implications for the guarantor...
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms where an individual other than the borrower is to provide a guarantee or indemnity in relation to a regulated deferred payment credit agreement

candidates.statement: In relation to regulated deferred payment credit agreements, firms must communicate as soon as possible after a customer has failed to make a payment by the time it has fallen due, providing information including any adverse consequences for the customer arising out of the missed payment.
candidates.sourceQuotation: Firms will be required to communicate with a borrower as soon as possible after they have failed to make a payment by the time it has fallen due... Any adverse consequences for the customer arising out of the missed payment. • Any other adverse consequences for the borrower that the firm considers are likely to arise out of the missed payment.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms when a customer has failed to make a payment under a regulated deferred payment credit agreement by the time it has fallen due

candidates.statement: Before terminating a regulated deferred payment credit agreement or taking steps to enforce a term of the agreement (by demanding earlier payment, restricting/terminating borrower rights, or enforcing security) where a customer is in arrears, firms must provide reasonable notice to the borrower and signpost to free and impartial money guidance and debt advice, effectively communicating the potential benefits of accessing it.
candidates.sourceQuotation: This requires firms to signpost to free and impartial money guidance and debt advice, and effectively communicate the potential benefits of accessing it, when giving a customer who is in arrears notice required under our rules before: • Terminating a DPC agreement; or • Taking steps to enforce a term of the agreement by demanding earlier payment of any sum, treating any right conferred on the debtor by the agreement as terminated, restricted or deferred, or enforcing any security.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies when a customer is in arrears under a regulated deferred payment credit agreement and the firm intends to terminate the agreement or take enforcement steps

candidates.statement: Information made available to customers must be provided in such a way that the customer can reasonably be expected to know how to access it and be able to access it. Information must be communicated so that the customer's attention is drawn to it and it is not disguised, diminished or obscured by other information, and in good time for the customer to consider it and make effective decisions before entering into the agreement.
candidates.sourceQuotation: For the purposes of this section, information is made available to a customer only if the customer can reasonably be expected to: (1) know how to access it; and (2) be able to access it... firms should ensure that the information required under this section is communicated: (a) in such a way that: (i) the customer's attention is drawn to it; and (ii) it is not disguised, diminished or obscured by any other information given to the customer at the same time; and (b) in good time for the customer to consider it and make effective decisions before entering into the agreement.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms providing information under CONC 4.2A in relation to regulated deferred payment credit agreements

candidates.statement: Firms with deferred payment credit activities will be subject to existing FCA regulatory reporting requirements, including Product Sales Data (PSD) returns, once they breach de minimis thresholds of either £2m in new advances or £2m in outstanding balances in a given year.
candidates.sourceQuotation: Overall, we received broad support for our proposals to apply our existing regulatory reporting requirements, including the PSD returns... However, PSD reporting requirements only apply once a firm breaches one of the de minimis thresholds in a given year. Specifically, either £2m in new advances or £2m in outstanding balances.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms with deferred payment credit activities once they breach de minimis thresholds of either £2m in new advances or £2m in outstanding balances in a given year

candidates.statement: Firms currently offering deferred payment credit intending to operate under temporary permission must notify the FCA of their desire to be registered for the Temporary Permissions Regime (TPR) during the notification window opening on 15 May 2026 and closing 2 weeks before Regulation Day (15 July 2026). Firms must pay a Category 1 fee and provide projections of annual income for future DPC activities and projections of the value of their DPC lending.
candidates.sourceQuotation: In line with the proposals in the CP, notification for registration for temporary permission will open 2 months before Regulation Day and close 2 weeks before Regulation Day... In CP25/33, we proposed that firms would need to pay a Category 1 fee to register for temporary permission... we proposed that firms provide the following information when notifying a desire for registration... A projection of annual income for future DPC activities. • Projections of the value of their DPC lending.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms currently offering deferred payment credit that intend to enter the Temporary Permissions Regime

candidates.statement: Firms with deferred payment credit temporary permission must be fully compliant with the Consumer Duty from Regulation Day (15 July 2026), including demonstrating fair value, delivering customer support and overall delivering good outcomes for retail customers.
candidates.sourceQuotation: Firms preparing to enter the TPR should begin planning early to ensure operational readiness for Regulation Day. In particular, firms should: • Make sure they are fully compliant with the Consumer Duty from Regulation Day. This includes demonstrating fair value, delivering customer support and overall delivering good outcomes for retail customers, as well as the other rules they will need to comply with.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms with deferred payment credit temporary permission from Regulation Day

candidates.statement: Firms with temporary permission must apply for full authorisation within the 6-month window directly following Regulation Day. Firms that do not apply within this window will lose their temporary permission.
candidates.sourceQuotation: Note that temporary permission is not indefinite. Firms will be able to apply for full authorisation before the end of the 6-month window directly following Regulation Day. Firms that do not apply within this window will lose their temporary permission.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to firms with deferred payment credit temporary permission who wish to continue operating beyond the temporary permission period

candidates.statement: Where a firm's permission comprises both Part 4A permission granted by the FCA and deferred payment credit temporary permission, the firm's deferred payment credit temporary permission is to be disregarded for the purposes of categorising what type of SMCR firm the firm is and for determining the application of SMCR provisions.
candidates.sourceQuotation: This rule applies where a firm's permission comprises permission to carry on regulated activities granted by the FCA under Part 4A of the Act and a deferred payment credit temporary permission. (2) The firm's deferred payment credit temporary permission is to be disregarded for the purposes of categorising what type of SMCR firm the firm is in accordance with SYSC 23 Annex 1...
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies where a firm's permission comprises both Part 4A permission granted by the FCA and deferred payment credit temporary permission

candidates.statement: In circumstances where the only regulated activities in a firm's permission are deferred payment credit activities permitted by a deferred payment credit temporary permission, the firm is not an SMCR firm.
candidates.sourceQuotation: In circumstances where the only regulated activities in a firm's permission are deferred payment credit activities permitted by a deferred payment credit temporary permission, a firm is not an SMCR firm (and is included in Part Three of SYSC 23 Annex 1 (Definition of exempt firm)).
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies where the only regulated activities in a firm's permission are deferred payment credit activities permitted by a deferred payment credit temporary permission

candidates.statement: Gibraltar-based firms carrying on deferred payment credit activity must comply with the relevant Handbook provisions relating to deferred payment credit activity, including the product information requirements in CONC 4.2A.
candidates.sourceQuotation: A Gibraltar-based firm carrying on deferred payment credit activity must comply with the relevant Handbook provisions relating to deferred payment credit activity... This section also applies to a Gibraltar-based firm with respect to deferred payment credit lending.
candidates.applicabilityConditions: Applies to Gibraltar-based firms carrying on deferred payment credit activity
